purpose: The DS envelope v1, replayed. Each case carries the command id, its contract version and either the data of a success or the refusal of an error, and the exact envelope both externals must emit: ds on stdout under --output json and the desktop shell to the webview. The kernel replays it through ds_command_kernel::envelope::{success, error} and ds-cli replays the same file through ds-cli-contract's success_envelope/error_envelope, so the answer shape cannot be true in one process and not the other. Byte-for-byte: member order is part of the contract, and every object under data and detail is written with its keys already in sorted order so a serializer that sorts maps and one that preserves insertion order emit the same bytes.
source: Transcribed from ds-cli/crates/ds-cli-contract/src/outcome.rs (ENVELOPE_VERSION, ExitClass::token and ::retryable, SuccessEnvelope, ErrorEnvelope, ErrorBody, success_envelope, error_envelope), 2026-09-17, under the owner's ruling that ds-cli is an external client exactly like Svelte: same id, same declared arg names, same DS envelope.
note: Re-record expected with DS_ENVELOPE_CASES_WRITE=1 cargo test --test envelope_cases after a deliberate envelope change, and say why in the commit; the envelope version is raised only for a breaking change to the envelope itself, never for a change inside data. remedy and detail are written only when the refusal carries them and next only when it names at least one command; retryable is a function of the class alone.

cases.why: A successful command answers exactly five members in this order, and data is carried as the command built it; here the preview row a desktop door and the CLI both project.
A command with nothing to say still answers an object under data, never null and never a missing member; a consumer reads data.x without a presence check first.
data is whatever JSON the command's contract declares, so a listing command answers an array there without wrapping it.
A contract version of zero is a legal number, not an absence: the envelope carries it as 0 and never omits it.
An internal refusal is not retryable and, carrying nothing but its three required members, the body ends at retryable: no null remedy, no empty next, no null detail.

refusal.message: the preview entry answered a page without a layout id

error.message: the preview entry answered a page without a layout id

cases.why: An internal refusal may still say what to do about it; remedy, next and detail are written in that order after retryable.

refusal.message: a command answered with no status
refusal.remedy: report this with the command you ran

error.message: a command answered with no status
error.remedy: report this with the command you ran

cases.why: An invalid invocation is the caller's to fix, so it is not retryable unchanged; a remedy alone is written between retryable and nothing else.

refusal.message: `--seed` is host-owned or not a preview argument on the desktop
refusal.remedy: pass only --transformer and --preview-layout with a preview

error.message: `--seed` is host-owned or not a preview argument on the desktop
error.remedy: pass only --transformer and --preview-layout with a preview

cases.why: A localised surface renders detail.message_key with detail.params instead of message; detail is carried exactly as the refusal built it, nested objects included.

error.message: the room for TX-0421 is still being stored on this computer
error.remedy: wait for the Design/Status page to finish storing the room

cases.why: An unknown command is refused before any contract is chosen: command is the closest thing to an id, contract 0, and the body ends at retryable false.
An unavailable engine is the world's to fix, so the class is retryable; next alone is written after retryable, with no remedy member at all.

refusal.message: the ds-report engine is not installed beside this executable

error.message: the ds-report engine is not installed beside this executable

cases.why: An unavailable refusal with everything: retryable true, then remedy, next and detail in that order.

error.message: the administrative boundary asset is not installed

cases.why: An unavailable refusal with nothing but its three members still answers retryable true, because the class alone decides it.

refusal.message: no desktop instance is running for this account

error.message: no desktop instance is running for this account

cases.why: An unauthorized refusal is not retryable; detail alone follows retryable directly, with neither remedy nor next written.

cases.why: An unauthorized refusal that says nothing more than its code and sentence.

cases.why: An unauthorized refusal with everything: retryable false, then remedy, next and detail in that order.

cases.why: A stale view is retryable once the world has moved; remedy and next are both written, and detail is absent.

cases.why: A conflict with everything, including an empty-object detail, which is still a present member because the refusal carried one.

cases.why: A refusal that names no next command carries an empty list in memory but the envelope omits the member; an absent next means nothing to run, not a null.
